# The "Magpies"
The [bold]Military Organization for Development and Innovation[/bold] (MODI), known to the average servicemember as the [bold]Magpies[/bold], is a loose coalition within the UA's militaries united by profit and personal opportunity. It champions the corporations that arm them.
## History - MODI was founded by officers and officials involved in the USCM's creation in 2101, to secure the military's future through close ties with the companies that supply its guns, dropships and technology. - Unlike the other factions, it exists only within the UA's militaries. It is strongest in the [textlink="Colonial Marines" link="CMUGuideLoreUSCM"], whose suppliers are mostly MODI-aligned, while other branches lean on unaligned companies MODI distrusts. - Its leaders have traditionally been senior requisitions officers, the first to see how much the military depends on its suppliers.
## Ideology [italic]These are the faction's general attitudes. Members are loyal to many different sponsors, and two Magpies may disagree completely.[/italic] - [bold]Alignment[/bold]: politically varied. Members are aligned by potential personal gain. Corporate. - Protect the reputation and secrets of MODI-aligned companies. Obscure and destroy physical evidence. - Everyone has their own connections. Don't look too closely at anyone else's. - Disputes between different interests are not MODI's problem. If feuding members draw attention, MODI will disown them all. - Proving your dedication to MODI's sponsors can bring money, promotions and other rewards.
## Internal Divisions MODI has more internal factions than any other. Megacorporations compete with each other, smaller arms makers fight to avoid being swallowed up, and UA government-owned companies try to hold their ground against foreign rivals such as [textlink="Weyland-Yutani" link="CMUGuideLoreWY"]. Its known sub-factions include the Modernisation and Development Organization, the Conglomerate Cooperative, the Industry and Development Cooperative, the Industry and Manufacturing Cooperative and the Corporate Cooperative.
## Reputation - Requisitions officers, logistics commanders and ambitious career officers support it widely, drawn by its promise of fast promotions, generous benefits and comfortable jobs after service. - Many frontline troops and traditionalist officers see it as self-serving and compromised, and fear that its ties to foreign megacorporations put the military's assets in the hands of companies that don't share the UA's interests. - MODI has helped make the UA's militaries, the USCM above all, some of the best-armed forces in human space. By lobbying hard and cutting through the slow procurement process, it gets prototype weapons into combat long before they are formally approved, such as the XM88 heavy rifle, first proven in the Favela Wars. - That speed has a cost. Favored units get the newest gear while others make do with old equipment, and untested weapons have caused accidents and needless casualties. Critics fear promotions and resources are handed out by corporate loyalty rather than merit.
## Relations MODI sits on a different axis from the other two factions, and has members who share the views of both. It plays each side individually: the [textlink="Doves" link="CMUGuideLoreUADoves"] want its non-weapon technology for their humanitarian work, and the [textlink="Hawks" link="CMUGuideLoreUAHawks"] want its cutting-edge arms, even as both worry about its corporate influence. Too divided to take over the others, MODI is content to keep the balance.
